turns.final_output:
The morning-after pill, also known as emergency contraception, is a medication designed to prevent pregnancy after unprotected sexual intercourse or contraceptive failure. It is most effective when taken within 72 hours following the event, although some formulations may be effective up to 120 hours post-intercourse. Common options include I-pill and Unwanted 72, which are typically administered as a single dose. Side effects may include mild cramps and irregular bleeding, which can occur as the body adjusts to the hormonal changes induced by the pill. For personalized advice and guidance, consulting a healthcare professional is recommended.

The I-pill, an emergency contraceptive, is most effective when taken as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse, ideally within 72 hours. It is designed to prevent pregnancy by delaying ovulation or inhibiting fertilization. If taken within 24 hours, the efficacy is highest. It is important to note that side effects such as nausea, vomiting, and changes in menstrual cycles may occur. If your period is delayed beyond a week after taking the I-pill, it is advisable to take a pregnancy test and consult a healthcare professional for further guidance.
